facts.fact: Blender's current manual (5.3 page) describes Size (Width, Height) as an alternative to focal length for setting field of view, useful for matching a physical camera and lens, e.g. for motion tracking.
Blender camera Sensor Fit options: Auto uses the larger Resolution dimension to define a square sensor; Horizontal sets sensor width manually and derives height from the output aspect ratio.
Background image Fit scales the image to fit inside the camera view without changing aspect ratio; Crop scales it to fill the camera view, cutting off part of the image.

For matching real footage, sensor width should come from the camera's spec sheet; in Python, Camera.sensor_width and sensor_height are in millimeters, and the Camera Info geometry node outputs sensor size as a 2D vector in mm.

Blender developers proposed replacing View-panel background images with Image Empties starting in 2.8x (proposal issue #52668); the camera-view drawing function was suggested to move into the camera data-block. This is a proposal, not confirmed as shipped behavior.
Image empties are drawn in perspective and orthographic views; the camera background remains the mechanism for drawing in camera view with framing options, per tracker discussion summaries.

Tracker issue #120929 reports Blender did not render a camera background image or movie clip during animation renders; developers treated the use of image empties as the reason, per the search summary.

Tracker reports exist for camera-background regressions: T98875 (adding a camera background image shows an 'Image not found' error) and T44096 (background image size/offset has no effect in camera view).
Add an Image Empty in Blender 2.8+: Shift+A > Empty > Image, settings in Object Data Properties; per a third-party guide, the Image Empty and Image Object differ only in the underlying datablocks.

fSpy is an open-source, cross-platform still-image camera matching app that computes approximate focal length, orientation and position from user-placed control points and vanishing lines; the usual path is exporting the camera to Blender.
fSpy is the author's stand-alone successor to the Blender add-on BLAM (Per Gantelius's announcement on Blender Artists).

The fSpy-Blender importer reads principal point, horizontal field of view and image dimensions from the .fspy project JSON and rejects project files whose version is not 1 (per the search summary of fspy.py).

A third-party benchmark reported .fspy files imported with fSpy-Blender gave the same camera matrix as its own output (maximum difference 1.4e-7) and the same field of view; .fspy files do not store vanishing points.

fSpy-Blender open issue #89 (Sept 2025) asks whether the importer works in Blender 4.5; open issue #88 reports matching fails with strong vanishing points. Both were seen only as titles in a search summary, not verified on the issue pages.
The perspective-match Blender extension states its solver is a port of fSpy's solver (GPL-3.0) and that its Blender camera mapping follows the fSpy importer.
fSpy struggles when an image has no clear vanishing points; the V-Sekai decision record suggests alternative methods in that case.
Vanishing-point workflows use one to three vanishing points depending on how many sets of parallel lines an image shows (Packt, 3D Environment Design with Blender; tutorial statement, not a study).
GeoCalib (arXiv 2409.06704, 2024) authors describe classical vanishing-point geometry as accurate but not robust, motivating learned single-image calibration.
Perspective Fields for Single Image Camera Calibration (CVPR 2023) is a learned single-image calibration method; its abstract was not read in this run.
fSpy issue #119 is a feature idea for basic reference shapes (e.g. known-size objects) to help focal-length matching; issue #53 asks about zoom on the image.

contradictions: Blender manual (5.3) frames camera Size/sensor as the field-of-view control, while older 2.79 pages and developer discussions describe a separate View-panel background-image workflow; the developer proposal (#52668) argues background images should be replaced by image empties, so the 'right' place for reference photos depends on Blender version.
fSpy-Blender README-level claims of working with Blender 4.x/5.x are not confirmed: issue #89 asks whether it works in 4.5 and is open.
